valuationInputs.name: Beta
valuationInputs.reason: 8 steps, 25 Nov 2026. (1) Business: two segments, hand protection (rubber gloves made in Sri Lanka and Thailand, 63% of 2025/26 segment operating profit, Rs 4.515bn) and plantations (tea and rubber through Kelani Valley, Talawakelle and Horana Plantations, 37%, Rs 2.627bn) (Annual Report 2025/26, note 30.2, p. 556). (2) Damodaran's emerging-markets dataset (betaEmerg) couldn't be reached from this run (pages.stern.nyu.edu blocked). Stand-ins: his global unlevered betas corrected for cash, January 2026, from web-search extracts: Rubber & Tires 0.78 (91 firms) for gloves, Farming/Agriculture 0.49 (the figure Chemical Industries and Bairaha Farms used). Weighted 63/37: 0.673. (3) Relevered with net debt Rs 16.24bn at 30 Sep 2026 (borrowings 19.797 + leases 2.704 − cash 6.259, Interim to 30 Sep 2026, p. 6) ÷ market value Rs 35.74bn (598.6mn shares × Rs 59.70, last trade 30 Sep 2026) = 0.45, at the 2025/26 tax rate of 32.4%: 0.673 × (1 + 0.676 × 0.45) = 0.88. (4) No local 5-year beta found by web search. (5) So 0.88. (6) Within 0.3–2. (7) Cost of equity from scripts/reinvestment.py. (8) Shown in the Required return tile. Refresh in January 2027 with the emerging-markets file.

valuationInputs.name: WACC
valuationInputs.reason: scripts/reinvestment.py, 25 Nov 2026: cost of debt 6.56% (interest paid Rs 0.972bn ÷ average borrowings and leases Rs 14.81bn, 2025/26; low because much of the debt is in dollars, baht and euros, and the report's capitalisation rate is 7.70%), tax 32.4%, debt weight 31.2% at Rs 59.70.

valuationInputs.name: Growth check
valuationInputs.value: Assumed 3% / 6% / 8%; supported 27.9% by the calculator, 6.4% on profit kept × ROE
valuationInputs.reason: The calculator's 27.9% comes from a 2025/26 reinvestment rate of 210% (capex Rs 7.78bn against depreciation Rs 3.09bn, plus Rs 4.99bn more working capital) and isn't a steady figure. Profit kept × ROE (63.8% × 10.1%) = 6.4%: all scenarios within 2 points (bull 1.6 above, backed by the Katunayake plant under construction and the W3 plant opened in April 2025).

valuationInputs.name: Growth
valuationInputs.reason: Hand protection revenue +10% in 2025/26 and +22% in April–September 2026 on new capacity (W3 Hanwella, Hi-Care Thailand); plantations −6% and +4% on weather and tea and rubber prices. Group revenue grew 3% in 2025/26 and 16% in the half. Base 6% ≈ the supported 6.4%.

valuationInputs.name: Return on new capital
valuationInputs.reason: 2025/26 after-tax operating profit Rs 4.60bn ÷ opening owners' equity plus net debt Rs 34.7bn = 13.3% (calculator). Company ROE 10–15% in the last three years, 24% in 2021/22–2022/23.

valuationInputs.name: Long-term growth
valuationInputs.reason: About nominal growth; below the 12.24% bond yield and WACC.

valuationInputs.name: Long-run ROE
valuationInputs.reason: Company ROE 24.6%, 24.1%, 15.5%, 12.2%, 10.1% in 2021/22–2025/26 (decade at a glance, p. 570), five-year average 17.3%; twelve months to Sep 2026 12.6%. Base 14% assumes hand protection keeps improving while plantations stay weak.

valuationInputs.name: EPS to March 2027
valuationInputs.reason: Six months Rs 4.59 plus a second half of Rs 2.9 / 4.3 / 5.0. Run-rate Rs 10.12 (Sep quarter Rs 2.53 × 4; twelve months Rs 7.46). Base 12% below it because the September quarter's tax was only 18% of profit before tax (32% in 2025/26): at a 30% rate the quarter is about Rs 2.17, × 4 = Rs 8.7. Bear repeats last year's second half (Rs 2.87).

valuationInputs.name: Dividend to March 2027
valuationInputs.reason: Interims Rs 0.37 + 0.96 = Rs 1.33 already paid for 2026/27 (Rs 0.86 a year earlier); 2025/26 total Rs 2.13 (36% of EPS). About 30% of the EPS cases.

valuationInputs.name: Maintenance capex basis
valuationInputs.value: depreciation (base, bull); middle of the range (bear)
valuationInputs.reason: No company split. 2025/26 capex booked Rs 7.78bn against depreciation and amortisation Rs 3.09bn: the report calls it one of its biggest investment programmes (Katunayake greenfield plant, W3 Hanwella, Kottawa and Hanwella Rubber capacity), so most of it is growth, but no amounts are given for the named projects. Base and bull use depreciation (Rs 3.09bn); bear uses the calculator's middle (Rs 4.59bn) in case more of it is upkeep. Formers (moulds) are left out of both capex and depreciation because their wear (impairment of formers, Rs 0.15bn) is already charged in operating profit.

valuationInputs.name: Investments less minorities (add-on)
valuationInputs.reason: The DCF values the whole group, so the non-controlling interests' share (mostly minorities in the plantation companies and Hanwella Rubber) comes off at book, Rs 9.013bn, and the other non-current financial assets (fixed deposits, a Singer Finance subordinated trust, Martin Bauer Hayleys shares), whose income is outside operating profit, are added at book, Rs 3.353bn, both at 30 Sep 2026 (Interim, p. 6). (3.353 − 9.013) ÷ 598.6mn shares × 1000 (Rs bn to Rs a share).

valuationInputs.name: Methods used
valuationInputs.value: Whole-company DCF less minorities plus investments, P/E, justified price to book, residual income, dividend model
valuationInputs.reason: A manufacturer with steady operating cash before working capital, so a cash-flow DCF; owners' earnings methods use profit after minorities. NAV shown as a reading only: plantation land and bearer plants are at book or revaluation, and much of it belongs to minorities.

openQuestions: December 2026 quarter: does glove segment profit keep growing 40%+, and does the tax rate stay near 20% or return to about 30%?
Working capital: do receivables (Rs 22.6bn at Sep 2026) and short-term loans (Rs 12.65bn) come down, so cash after capex covers dividends again?
Katunayake greenfield plant: cost, start date and capacity (not given in the annual report).
Plantations: segment profit fell 17% in April–September 2026; watch wages, tea and rubber prices.
Net debt Rs 16.24bn at Sep 2026: watch whether it keeps rising.
Beta: refresh with Damodaran's emerging-markets file and any local 5-year beta in January 2027.
Annual report 2026/27: record capex booked, depreciation, working capital and any amounts for named growth projects.

changeLog.summary: Requested from Telegram (/add DIPD.N0000). First analysis, from the downloaded annual report 2025/26 and the interims to June and September 2026.
